title: Determinants
summary: |a b; c d| = ad − bc. A 3 × 3 determinant is expanded along any row or column: Δ = a₁₁C₁₁ + a₁₂C₁₂ + a₁₃C₁₃.
Minor Mᵢⱼ: the determinant left after deleting row i and column j. Cofactor Cᵢⱼ = (−1)^(i+j) Mᵢⱼ.

(1) |A'| = |A|. (2) Interchanging two rows changes the sign. (3) Two identical (or proportional) rows make Δ = 0. (4) A common factor of a row can be taken out, so |kA| = kⁿ|A| for an n × n matrix. (5) Adding a multiple of one row to another leaves Δ unchanged (R₁ → R₁ + kR₂). (6) A row of sums splits into two determinants only one row at a time.
A skew-symmetric determinant of odd order is 0, because |A| = |A'| = |−A| = −|A|.
Area of a triangle = ½|x₁ y₁ 1; x₂ y₂ 1; x₃ y₃ 1|. The points are collinear when this determinant is 0.
A is singular if |A| = 0 and non-singular if |A| ≠ 0.
Cube roots of unity: 1 + w + w² = 0 and w³ = 1 — use them to simplify determinants containing w.

mcq.work:
Expand: 1(1 − w²) − w²(w² − w³) + w²(w³ − w²).
With w³ = 1: 1 − w² − w²(w² − 1) + w²(1 − w²) = 1 − w² − w⁴ + w² + w² − w⁴ = 1 + w² − 2w (w⁴ = w).
= (1 + w + w²) − 3w = −3w.

objective: Fill in the blanks: (a) If A is a square matrix of order 2, |kA| = ______. (b) If x ∈ N and |x + 3 −2; −3x 2x| = 8, then x = ______.
objective4: True or False: (a) Matrix A is singular if |A| ≠ 0. (b) |a+b c+d; e+f g+h| = |a c; e g| + |b d; f h|. (c) Interchanging two rows changes the sign of a determinant. (d) The determinant of a 3 × 3 skew-symmetric matrix is 0.

(a) False — singular means |A| = 0.
(b) False — a determinant splits along one row (or column) at a time only.
(c) True.
(d) True — |A| = |A'| = |−A| = −|A| ⇒ |A| = 0.
vsa: Without expanding, prove that |0 a −b; −a 0 −c; b c 0| = 0.

Let Δ be the determinant. Its transpose has every element negated (it is skew-symmetric), so Δ = |A'| = |−A| = (−1)³Δ = −Δ.
Hence 2Δ = 0 ⇒ Δ = 0.
Show that |1 a bc; 1 b ca; 1 c ab| = (a − b)(b − c)(c − a).

R₁ → R₁ − R₂, R₂ → R₂ − R₃:
|0 a−b c(b−a); 0 b−c a(c−b); 1 c ab| = (a − b)(b − c)|0 1 −c; 0 1 −a; 1 c ab|.
Expand along C₁: 1 × (1·(−a) − (−c)·1) = c − a.
So Δ = (a − b)(b − c)(c − a).
If A = [[sin x, 1, 1], [1, eˣ, 1], [cos x, 0, 1]], show that |4A| = 64|A|.
Each of the 3 rows has the factor 4 taken out: |4A| = 4³|A| = 64|A|.
Prove that |−a² ab ac; ab −b² bc; ac bc −c²| = 4a²b²c².

Take a, b, c from R₁, R₂, R₃ and a, b, c from C₁, C₂, C₃: Δ = a²b²c² |−1 1 1; 1 −1 1; 1 1 −1|.
= a²b²c² [−1(1 − 1) − 1(−1 − 1) + 1(1 + 1)] = a²b²c²(0 + 2 + 2) = 4a²b²c².
Expand along R₁: −1 × (x·x − x·1) = −(x² − x) = 0 ⇒ x(x − 1) = 0 ⇒ x = 0 or 1.
sa: Using determinants, check whether (a, b + c), (b, c + a) and (c, a + b) form a triangle.

Δ = |a b+c 1; b c+a 1; c a+b 1|. C₁ → C₁ + C₂: every entry of C₁ becomes a + b + c.
Δ = (a + b + c)|1 b+c 1; 1 c+a 1; 1 a+b 1| = 0 (C₁ = C₃).
The area is 0, so the points are collinear and do not form a triangle.

or:
C₁ → C₁ + C₂ + C₃: C₁ becomes 5x + 4 in every row. Take it out.
R₂ → R₂ − R₁, R₃ → R₃ − R₁: |1 2x 2x; 0 4−x 0; 0 0 4−x|.
Δ = (5x + 4)(4 − x)².

la: Using properties of determinants, prove |a−b−c 2a 2a; 2b b−c−a 2b; 2c 2c c−a−b| = (a + b + c)³.

R₁ → R₁ + R₂ + R₃: R₁ becomes (a + b + c, a + b + c, a + b + c). Take (a + b + c) out:
Δ = (a + b + c)|1 1 1; 2b b−c−a 2b; 2c 2c c−a−b|.
C₂ → C₂ − C₁, C₃ → C₃ − C₁: |1 0 0; 2b −(a+b+c) 0; 2c 0 −(a+b+c)|.
Expand along R₁: (a + b + c) × (a + b + c)² = (a + b + c)³.
